messages.subject: bug in m*ply with global variables
messages.subject_clean: bug in m*ply with global variables
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

Consider the following code,

x = 5
y = 2

foo <- function(a="x"){
 switch(a, "x" = x,
              "y" = y)
  }

params <- expand.grid(a=c("y","x"))

mdply(params, foo)

  a V1
1 y  5
2 x  2

As far as I can see it's a bug (which I noticed, very puzzled, when
two facets of my ggplot had their labels swapped...)

The reason I'm doing this switch() construct is that I need to pass
data.frames to the function through mdply, so I just pass their name.

Thanks,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: A simplequestion
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

Is this supposed to be a question or an attempted answer? If the latter, what is the context?

Since z didn't work, I'll presume this is an alleged question. a/dcast (which BTW, is in the reshape2 package that you failed to mention) creates a tabular output display not too dissimilar in spirit to xtabs() from the base package, so the aggregation function has to return a *scalar* for each row/column combination - you're trying to return a vector. This requires you use something like ddply() instead:

library(plyr)
ddply(x, .(I), summarise, n = length(V), mean = mean(V), median = median(V))
  I n     mean median
1 a 2 2.000000      2
2 b 3 5.333333      5

Is that what you wanted?

Dennis

Hi,

On Thu, Mar 10, 2011 at 2:55 AM, prabh <harshapra...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I have  10 data sets of size 70MB each. I need to combine them to one
> single file and then do some analysis how do i do this in R.

(i) If they are in text files, you can always combine the text files
first (via `cat` or some other means).
(ii) You can `rbind` them together in R, assuming they are a data.frame

Also -- this is a general R question, so after you try those things
above and maybe think about a few other ways on your own, you can post
a followup question on R-help with some examples of what you tried to
do, and some error messages that show why what you try didn't work if
you still need help.

-steve

messages.subject: plyr, .parallel, .progress, R gui 2.12.2
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

In R 2.12.2, one can register/use a parallel backend in R gui. plyr
supports the parallel backend using .parallel.

I doubt that its recommended to use .progress alongside .parallel, but
in R term that just mean that the text progress bar goes till
(100/cores)%. Which is useful enough as I know how many cores there
are in the machine. With R gui, I find that if I do some thing like

## code start
## post loading libraries and registering back end

ddply(baseball, .(year), "nrow", .parallel=TRUE)

## code end

then I am fine. But,

## code start

ddply(baseball, .(year), "nrow", .parallel=TRUE, .progress="text")

## code end

hangs indefinitely in R gui (still works as "expected" in R term, bar
goes to 50%.)

I am not particularly advocating fixing .progress (I have no idea how
much work that would take). Its nice to be able to guesstimate how
long a break one can take ... waiting for the code to get done. But
not essential.

But it would be nice to quit gracefully (or ignore one of the flags)
if both flags are called in R gui. Maybe a simple fix is to always
ignore one of the flags if both are called. I know I spent a while
trying to work out why my code was hanging and then finally realized
that turning off the progress flag fixed things.

Just a thought.

Best,
Anirban

messages.subject: Null .margins bug
messages.body_plain:
The "The split-apply-combine strategy for data analysis" paper says:

> The fourth way is to not split up the matrix at all, and corresponds to .margins = c().
>
But there appears to be a bug in the .margins=c() case:

aaply(matrix(1:4,2,2),.margins=c(),print)
Error in names(split_labels) <- paste("X", seq_along(.margins), sep = "") :
  'names' attribute [1] must be the same length as the vector [0]

plyr 1.4 on R 2.12.2, Windows 7
